content: 1. Magnesium citrate reduces the absorption of demeclocycline in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the absorption of demeclocycline in the gastrointestinal tract, resulting in reduced drug levels. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapy. 3. Magnesium oxide inhibits the gastrointestinal absorption of demeclocycline, lowering its levels. This interaction is relevant only to oral forms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Magnesium sulfate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies to oral forms only. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Magnesium supplements can decrease the levels or effects of demeclocycline by forming an insoluble complex that reduces drug absorption in the intestinal tract. To minimize this interaction, administer magnesium at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after demeclocycline. Monitor therapy closely. 6. Demeclocycline can reduce the effectiveness of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Demeclocycline increases methotrexate levels by reducing its elimination. Tetracyclines may interfere with methotrexate metabolism by inhibiting intestinal flora and enterohepatic circulation. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 8. Co-administration of demeclocycline and methoxsalen may increase the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly through additive photosensitizing effects. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Demeclocycline and methoxyflurane should not be used together due to the risk of nephrotoxicity caused by pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Demeclocycline and methyl aminolevulinate may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly by enhancing photosensitizing effects. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of oral microbiota products by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of bacterial spore-containing microbiota products. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 12. Demeclocycline and mipomersen may increase each other’s toxicity by elevating hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. Use caution or consider alternative therapy. 13. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Demeclocycline decreases niacin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 15. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Demeclocycline and palovarotene should not be used together due to the risk of benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) associated with systemic retinoid use and tetracyclines. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Demeclocycline increases pancuronium’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Demeclocycline decreases pantothenic acid levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 19. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Demeclocycline increases phenindione’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 22. Demeclocycline reduces piperacillin’s effectiveness by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 23. Polycarbophil reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Polysaccharide iron reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Demeclocycline and porfimer may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly by enhancing photosensitivity. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Demeclocycline increases protamine’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 27. Demeclocycline decreases pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 28. Demeclocycline increases rapacuronium’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Demeclocycline increases rocuronium’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Rose hips reduce demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Sodium bicarbonate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer sodium bicarbonate at least 2 hours apart from demeclocycline. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Sodium citrate/citric acid reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer sodium citrate at least 2 hours apart from demeclocycline. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid reduces demeclocycline levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents to avoid magnesium chelation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Strontium ranelate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This combination is contraindicated. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 36. Demeclocycline increases succinylcholine’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 37. Sucralfate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 38. Demeclocycline reduces temocillin’s effectiveness by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Demeclocycline decreases thiamine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 40. Demeclocycline and tretinoin should not be used together due to increased phototoxicity caused by pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Demeclocycline and topical tretinoin should not be used together due to increased phototoxicity caused by pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. Use caution and monitor therapy. 43. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 44. Demeclocycline reduces the effectiveness of the live typhoid vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 45. Demeclocycline reduces vasopressin’s effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 46. Demeclocycline increases vecuronium’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Demeclocycline and verteporfin may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly by enhancing phototoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 48. Demeclocycline increases warfarin’s effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 49. Zinc reduces demeclocycline levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or after zinc salts. Use caution and monitor therapy. 50. Demeclocycline is associated with photosensitivity reactions, reversible dose-related diabetes insipidus, tooth discoloration, superinfection, dysphagia, glossitis, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hepatotoxicity, and hypersensitivity reactions. It forms stable calcium complexes in bone-forming tissues, potentially affecting growth in premature infants. Tetracyclines cross the placenta and may cause fetal toxicity, including skeletal development retardation. In patients with renal impairment, demeclocycline may lead to azotemia, hyperphosphatemia, and acidosis. Photosensitivity reactions, including severe sunburn, can occur. Pseudotumor cerebri has been reported, with symptoms such as headache and blurred vision. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, including fungi, may occur. Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported and may range from mild to fatal. Avoid demeclocycline during pregnancy.
